5.6.4 External cooling water system – Miscellaneous items Piping Coolant additives may attack a zinc layer. It is therefore imperative to avoid using galvanised steel pipes. Treatment of cooling water as specified by Everl- lence will safely protect the inner pipe walls against corrosion. Moreover, there is the risk of the formation of local electrolytic element couples where the zinc layer has been worn off, and the risk of aeration corro- sion where the zinc layer is not properly bonded to the substrate. See the working instructions 6682 000.16-01E for cleaning of steel pipes be- fore fitting. Pipes shall be manufactured and assembled in a way that ensures a proper draining of all segments. Venting is to be provided at each high point of the pipe system and drain openings at each low point.

is determined by the amount of remaining calcium and magnesium salts (sul- phates). Protective measures Anticorrosive agents contain chemical compounds that can pose a risk to health or the environment if incorrectly used. Comply with the directions in the manufacturer's material safety data sheets. Avoid prolonged direct contact with the skin. Wash hands thoroughly after use. If larger quantities spray and/or soak into clothing, remove and wash clothing before wearing it again. If chemicals come into contact with your eyes, rinse them immediately with plenty of water and seek medical advice. Anticorrosive agents are generally harmful to the water cycle. Observe the relevant statutory requirements for disposal. Auxiliary engines If the same cooling water system used in a MAN Diesel & Turbo two-stroke main engine is used in a marine engine of type 16/24, 21/ 31, 23/30H, 27/38 or 28/32H, the cooling water recommendations for the main engine must be observed.

the systems have been designed so that one of the engines can be equipped with a cooling system for ICS-operation (Integrated Charge air System). Fresh water treatment The engine cooling water is, like fuel oil and lubricat- ing oil, a medium which must be carefully selected, treated, maintained and monitored. Otherwise, corrosion, corrosion fatigue and cavita- tion may occur on the surfaces of the cooling sys- tem which are in contact with the water, and deposits may form. Corrosion and cavitation may reduce the life time and safety factors of parts concerned, and deposits will impair the heat transfer and may result in ther- mal overload of the components to be cooled. The treatment process of the cooling water has to be effected before the first commission of the plant, i.e. immediately after installation at the shipyard or at the power plant.

is determined by the amount of remaining calcium and magnesium salts (sul- phates). The temporary (carbonate) hardness is the critical factor that deter- mines the extent of limescale deposit in the cooling system. Water with a total hardness of > 10°dGH must be mixed with distilled water or softened. Subsequent hardening of extremely soft water is only necessary to prevent foaming if emulsifiable slushing oils are used. Damage to the cooling water system Corrosion is an electrochemical process that can widely be avoided by selecting the correct water quality and by carefully handling the water in the engine cooling system. Flow cavitation can occur in areas in which high flow velocities and high tur- bulence is present. If the steam pressure is reached, steam bubbles form and subsequently collapse in high pressure zones which causes the destruc- tion of materials in constricted areas.

The total hardness of the water is the combined effect of the temporary and permanent hardness. The proportion of calcium and magnesium salts is of overriding importance. Ad 4) The systems have been designed in such a way that the change-over from sea operation to harbour operation/stand-by with preheating can be made with a minimum of manual or automatic interference. Fresh water treatment The engine cooling water is, like fuel oil and lubricating oil, a medium which must be carefully selected, treated, maintained and monitored. The total hardness of the water is the combined effect of the temporary and permanent hardness. The proportion of calcium and magnesium salts is of overriding importance. The temporary hardness is determined by the carbo- nate content of the calcium and magnesium salts. The permanent hardness is determined by the amount of remaining calcium and magnesium salts (sul- phates). The temporary (carbonate) hardness is the critical factor that deter- mines the extent of limescale deposit in the cooling system. Water with a total hardness of > 10°dGH must be mixed with distilled water or softened. Subsequent hardening of extremely soft water is only necessary to prevent foaming if emulsifiable slushing oils are used. The cylinder head, cooling water jacket and top land ring can be drained together.

that are more than twice as high as recommended should be avoided. Every 2 to 6 months, a coolant sample must be sent to an independent labor- atory or to the engine manufacturer for an integrated analysis. If chemical additives or antifreeze agents are used, coolant should be re- placed after 3 years at the latest. If there are high concentrations of solids (rust), the water must be completely changed and the entire system must be carefully cleaned. Deposits in the cooling system can be caused by liquids penetrating the coolant, the emulsion breaking up, corrosion in the system, and limescale de- posits due to high water hardness. An increase in the content of chloride ions is generally an indication of seawater ingress.

Protective measures Anticorrosive agents contain chemical compounds that can pose a risk to health or the environment if incorrectly used. Comply with the directions in the manufacturer's material safety data sheets. Avoid prolonged direct contact with the skin. Wash hands thoroughly after use. If larger quantities spray and/or soak into clothing, remove and wash clothing before wearing it again. If chemicals come into contact with your eyes, rinse them immediately with plenty of water and seek medical advice. Anticorrosive agents are generally harmful to the water cycle. Observe the rel- evant statutory requirements for disposal. Auxiliary engines If the same cooling water system used in a Everllence two-stroke main engine is used in a marine engine of type 16/24, 21/ 31, 23/30H, 27/38 or 28/32H, the cooling water recommendations for the main engine must be observed.

Cooling water that is not treated properly may cause serious corrosion during storage or operation of the engine. LT = Low temperature HT = High temperature Cooler dimensioning, gen- eral For coolers operated by seawater (not treated water), lube oil or DMA/DMB on the primary side and treated freshwater on the secondary side, an addi- tional safety margin of 10% related to the heat transfer coefficient is to be considered. In case antifreeze is added to the cooling water, the corresponding lower heat transfer is to be taken into consideration.

6.6.4 External cooling water system – Miscellaneous items Piping Coolant additives may attack a zinc layer. It is therefore imperative to avoid using galvanised steel pipes. Treatment of cooling water as specified by Everl- lence will safely protect the inner pipe walls against corrosion. Moreover, there is the risk of the formation of local electrolytic element couples where the zinc layer has been worn off, and the risk of aeration corro- sion where the zinc layer is not properly bonded to the substrate. See the working instructions 6682 000.16-01E for cleaning of steel pipes be- fore fitting. Pipes shall be manufactured and assembled in a way that ensures a proper draining of all segments. Venting is to be provided at each high point of the pipe system and drain openings at each low point.

Emulsifiable slushing oils are used less and less frequently as their use has been considerably restricted by environmental protection regulations, and be- cause they are rarely available from suppliers for this and other reasons. Treatment prior to initial commissioning of engine Treatment with an anticorrosive agent should be carried out before the engine is brought into operation for the first time to prevent irreparable initial damage. Note: The engine must not be brought into operation without treating the cooling water first. Antifreeze agents reduce the capacity of the coolant to absorb heat. In some cases the cooling effect of the coolant may not be sufficient for certain opera- tion conditions. Antifreeze agents If temperatures below the freezing point of water in the engine cannot be ex- cluded, an antifreeze agent that also prevents corrosion must be added to the cooling system or corresponding parts. Otherwise, the entire system must be heated. Sufficient corrosion protection can be provided by adding the products listed in the table entitled Antifreeze agent with slushing properties (Military specific- ation: Federal Armed Forces Sy-7025), while observing the prescribed min- imum concentration. This concentration prevents freezing at temperatures down to –22 °C and provides sufficient corrosion protection. However, the quantity of antifreeze agent actually required always depends on the lowest temperatures that are to be expected at the place of use. Antifreeze agents are generally based on ethylene glycol.

See the working instructions 6682 000.16-01E for cleaning of steel pipes be- fore fitting. Pipes shall be manufactured and assembled in a way that ensures a proper draining of all segments. Venting is to be provided at each high point of the pipe system and drain openings at each low point.

Although the channel type keel cooling system discussed so far provides advantages over seawater cooling by eliminating silt/sand build-up and protecting against corrosion, their bulk size and location can reduce a vessel’s capacity and increase its drag. They are also prone to seaweed fouling. A more compact and streamlined keel cooler can be provided with a packaged type keel cooler as shown in Figure 31. Typical Packaged Keel Cooler Figure 31 Packaged keel coolers are purchased as prefabricated units and mounted to the outside of a ship’s hull. Manufacturers offer keel coolers in many configurations. Another important advantage of packaged keel coolers is their compactness and lightweight when compared to fabricated keel coolers.

Suggestions for Design of a Successful Central Cooling System • Flow Control: There are upper and lower limits to the allowable flow through an engine. The system must be able to throttle the flow through each engine independently.

• Temperature Control: The heat exchanger must be capable of delivering the proper amount of cooling, proportional to engine load. • Load Control: The amount of external water flow through a Cat Engine is directly proportional to the engine’s load. The greater the load, the greater the amount of cooling required and the more water the engine’s internal cooling circuitry will discharge for cooling. At light loads, the engine’s temperature controls will bypass the external portion of the engine cooling system, recirculating virtually all of the coolant. If the water pressure presented to an engine by a central cooling system is too high, the proper operation of the engine’s temperature controls may be overridden, and the engine will suffer over or under cooling problems.

MAN Energy Solutions B 52 00 0 L21/31;L27/38, 2016.09.28 - Diesel-electrical propulsion plants 7 (8) Data for external preheating system, item 39 High pressure from external cooling water pumps may disturb the preheating of the engine. In order to avoid this, it is in most cases necessary to install auto- matic shut off valve at cooling water inlet, which close when the engine is stopped. The capacity of the external preheater should be 3.0-3.5 kW/cyl. The flow through the engine should for each cylinder be approx. 4 l/min with flow from top and downwards and 25 l/min with flow from bottom and upwards. Different arrangements of central cooling systems There are many variations of centralised cooling systems and we are available to discuss various changes to suit an owner’s or builder’s specific wishes.

Additional HT preheating arrangement Charge air preheater arrangement for stand-alone dual fuel engines In some few cases issues of misfiring and related smoke emission have been observed during cold start. It has been found that the observed start issue is related to the general lower preheating level of the engine room in case of stand-alone engines. To prevent the cold start issues at stand-alone dual fuel engines it is recom- mended to install an external preheater with circulation pump. The preheater arrangement will support the cold start abilities by circulating preheated water through the charge air cooler before engine start. The external preheater unit with pump is to be installed in addition to the cool- ing water preheating arrangement built into the outlet pipe for the HT cooling water on the engine's front end.

High temperature preheater control box Figure 1: Dimensions of the control cabinet. The preheater control box is for controlling the electric heater built onto the engine for preheating of the engines jacket cooling water during stand-still. The control box consists of a cabinet with contactor and control system. On the front of the cabinet there is a lamp for "heater on" and a main switch for activating the system. Furthermore there is overload protection for the heater element. The temperature is controlled by means of an on/off thermostat mounted in the common HT-outlet pipe. Furthermore the system secures that the heater is activated only when the engine is in stand-still. Depending on the numbers of engines in the plant, the control box can be for one or several engines, however the dimensions of the cabinet will be the same. fig 1 illustrates a front for 3 engines.

Coolant Temperature Control The Tier 3 SCAC engines use inlet control temperature regulators/thermostats to provide uniform coolant temperature to the jacket water c ircuit and aftercooler circuit. The jacket water circuit has two regulators. The aftercooler circuit SCAC has one regulator. Treated Water Pumps The C32 Tier 3 Commercial Propulsion and Auxiliary engines have two gear -driven centrifugal water pumps mounted on the fro nt housing. The right -hand pump (viewed from the flywheel end) is the jacket water pump and supplies coolant to the oil cooler, block, and heads. The left -hand pump, referred to as the SCAC pump, supplies coolant to the fuel cooler and aftercooler. Each pump is equipped with pump covers that have two service ports available for measuring coolant temperature and pressure at pump inlet, and one service port on the pump housing for measuring at the pump outlet.

Combined Circuit Configuration The combined circuit configuration is often referred to as the single circuit — two pump system. It is typically used for diesel engine applications where a single radiator or heat exchanger is applied. The aftercooler circuit is externally regulated to nominal temperature (fluid inlet temperature control). The system uses the aftercooler outlet water to cool a portion of the high temperature outlet water to maintain nominal jacket water temperature to the cylinder block. The block is a closed circuit contained on the engine; therefore, only the water returning to the aftercooler pump requires a cooling source. This results in a relatively simple coolant piping installation. Refer to Figure 4 and Figure 5 for typical combined circuit schematics.

refer to the section on Design Criteria for Standard Temperature Systems in the section on Heat Recovery. G3500 The ability to produce steam or high temperature water is a necessity for some co-generation installations. See the Heat Recovery Section for more discussion. Attachment groups allow the G3500 engines to perform either task. With these attachments, the engines have a higher maximum outlet temperature for the jacket water. A customer supplied water pump maintains the appropriate water flow. The water leaving the engine can be flashed to steam in an external boiler or used in the liquid phase. Heat recovery from the exhaust can be combined with jacket water for greater heat recovery. With high temperature cooling, the oil cooler is separate from the jacket water circuit. The aftercooler circuit and the oil cooler circuit can be ordered either combined or separate.

If solenoid valves are used to control cooling water, position them upstream of the heat exchanger. pipe) that are submerged in the nearby cool water. Figure 21 shows an example of a typical submerged pipe cooling system. A concrete catch basin or tank should be placed in the source of the cooling water. This will help ensure a consistent volume of water around the coils and help keep mud and silt from burying the coils. The pipes must be supported up, off the bottom of the tank to ensure maximum cooling efficiency. Submerged Pipe Cooling System Figure 21 Engine heat rejection and the temperature of the cooling medium must be carefully considered in determining the correct amount of pipe to use. As a rule-of-thumb, 0.003 m (0.0353 ft2) of submerged pipe surface area is required for every 1.055 kJ/min (1 Btu/min) of jacket water heat rejection that must be removed. Engine type L/V engine Min. heating power (kW/cylinder) 14 Table 133: Heating power These values include the radiation heat losses from the outer surface of the engine. Also a margin of 20 % for heat losses of the cooling system has been considered. To prevent a too quick and uneven heating of the engine, the preheating tem- perature of the HT cooling water must remain mandatory below 90°C at en- gine inlet and the circulation amount may not exceed 30% of the nominal flow. The maximum heating power has to be calculated accordingly. A secondary function of the preheater is to provide heat capacity in the HT cooling water system during engine part load operation. This is required for marine propulsion plants with a high freshwater requirement, e.g. on passen- ger vessels, where frequent load changes are common.

HT cooling water preheating module (MOD-004) Before starting a cold engine, it is necessary to preheat the water jacket up to min. 60°C at engine outlet. For the total heating power required for preheating the HT cooling water from 10°C to 60°C within 4 hours see table Heating power, Page 379. Engine type L/V engine Min. heating power (kW/cylinder) 14 Table 158: Heating power These values include the radiation heat losses from the outer surface of the engine. Also a margin of 20 % for heat losses of the cooling system has been considered. To prevent a too quick and uneven heating of the engine, the preheating tem- perature of the HT cooling water must remain mandatory below 90°C at en- gine inlet and the circulation amount may not exceed 30% of the nominal flow. The maximum heating power has to be calculated accordingly.

E-HT-COMP-064 高温冷却水系统组成
A secondary function of the preheater is to provide heat capacity in the HT cooling water system during engine part load operation. This is required for marine propulsion plants with a high freshwater requirement, e.g. on passen- ger vessels, where frequent load changes are common. For engines operated in arctic conditions or with charge air from outside the vessel, the capacity of the preheater has to be increased. In this case contact Everllence. It is also required for arrangements with an additional charge air preheating by deviation of HT cooling water to the charge air cooler stage 2 (HE-008). In this case the heat output of the preheater is to be increased by approximately 50%. Avoid an installation of the preheater in parallel to the engine driven HT-pump. In this case, the preheater may not be operated while the engine is running.

An auxiliary oil cooler, e.g. a reverse gear oil cooler, can be connected to the keel cooling motor cooling system in the suction line between the coolant pipes and cool- ant pump intake. In some installations, it may be necessary to connect the auxiliary oil cooler to the bypass circuit to ensure coolant flow through the oil cooler when the thermostats are closed. An example of such an installation is where the engine load is low (which means low coolant temperature and long time before the thermostats open) or when using a reverse gear slipping valve to reduce propeller speed. If an auxiliary oil cool- ant is connected, an external thermostat must be fitted and the engine thermostat must be locked in the open position. Coolant Flow Control The external circuit resistance setting establishes the total circuit flow by balancing total circuit losses with the characteristic pump performance curves. Correct external resistance is very important. Too high a resistance will result in reduced flows to the aftercooler and/or jacket water circuit, causing their effectiveness to decrease. If there is too low a resistance, the fluid velocity may increase and exceed fluid velocity limits, and cavitation/early wear could be the result. The Pump Performance Curves in TMI illustrates the maximum recommended external resistance versus coolant flow at specific engine speeds.

Seawater Strainers Strainers are required in order to protect the seawater pump, aftercooler, heat exchanger and other cooling system components from foreign material in the seawater. The foreign material can plug and/or coat heat transfer surfaces, causing overheating of the engine and shortened life of components. If the foreign material is abrasive, it will erode pump impellers and soft metal parts, reducing their effectiveness. Seawater strainers should be installed below the water line and as close to the seawater inlet or sea chest as possible.

Keel cooling 02:05 Issue 8.0 en-GB 15 Keel cooling If the sea water is of such poor quality that it is not suitable for circulation through a sea water circuit, a keel cooling system can be installed. This may be suitable if, for example, the water has a high sludge or sand content or if there are contaminants or ice in the water that could block the sea water intake. The engine coolant is cooled by being circulated through pipe coils or cooling ele- ments mounted at the bottom of the vessel inside or outside the hull. On the Dl13 and DI16, the coolant for the charge air cooler may be cooled in a sep- arate circuit, depending on the engine power. MAN Diesel & Turbo 1694925-0.4 L27/38 12.31 Fig 6.7 Box cooling dia gram Box Cooler The box cooling system has through many years proven to be a reliable closed cooling water system. The box cooler is a pre-manufactured tube bundle for mounting in a sea chest. The movement of the sea water across the heat ex- changer is initiated by the movement of the heated sea water upwards because of the lower density compared with that of the surrounding water. This means that the heat transfer is less dependant on the ship’s speed, compared to coolers mounted on the shell of the vessel. However the speed of the vessel does have some influence on the cooling area. For vessels sailing at below 3 knots at MCR, i.e. tugs, dredgers etc, the speed has to be considered when designing the cooler. The temperature of the sea water has influence on the heat exchanger efficiency as well.

An aftercooler heat rejection factor is used to quantify the additional aftercooler heat rejection at altitude. A table of factors for various combinations of altitude and ambient temperature is typically provided with a gas engine technical data sheet. Engine operation under arctic conditions and at low load carries the risk of heat loss in the cooling water systems and resulting risk of engine operation problems or even damage. Therefore 3 cases are given: Case1 Preheating of the intake air of the engine to a minimum of 0°C. Case 2 Installation of adequate HT preheater, that operates in parallel to engine oper- ation to compensate HT energy losses. If operation within Range I is required, a) the preheater size within the plant must be capable to compensate any heat losses within the cooling water system and to keep these on the required temperature level. b) all preheaters need to be operated in parallel to engine operation until min- imum engine load is reached.

Corrosion Inhibitors A suitable corrosion inhibitor, carefully maintained, will minimize internal corrosive effects. See the section on Cooling System Protection. Box Coolers Box coolers represent another type of packaged cooler that is sometimes used in marine applications. As seen in Figure 32, box coolers are mounted inside a vessel’s sea chest. This location provides excellent protection from mechanical damage, but does negate the benefit that vessel speed through the water provides for keel cooler installations. However, box coolers, like keel coolers, eliminate the need for the raw water system associated with the use of inboard heat exchangers.

chunk_text:
E-COOLANT-CLEAN-033 冷却系统清洗要求
Lime and rust deposits Lime and rust deposits can form if the water is especially hard or if the con- centration of the anticorrosive agent is too low. A thin lime scale layer can be left on the surface as experience has shown that this protects against corro- sion. However, limescale deposits with a thickness of more than 0.5 mm ob- struct the transfer of heat and cause thermal overloading of the components being cooled. Rust that has been flushed out may have an abrasive effect on other parts of the system, such as the sealing elements of the water pumps. Together with the elements that are responsible for water hardness, this forms what is known as ferrous sludge which tends to gather in areas where the flow velo- city is low. E-COOLANT-CLEAN-033 冷却系统清洗要求
Lime and rust deposits Lime and rust deposits can form if the water is especially hard or if the con- centration of the anticorrosive agent is too low. A thin lime scale layer can be left on the surface as experience has shown that this protects against corro- sion. However, limescale deposits with a thickness of more than 0.5 mm ob- struct the transfer of heat and cause thermal overloading of the components being cooled. Rust that has been flushed out may have an abrasive effect on other parts of the system, such as the sealing elements of the water pumps. Together with the elements that are responsible for water hardness, this forms what is known as ferrous sludge which tends to gather in areas where the flow velo- city is low. This mild solvent must not be used in systems that have been neglected or have heavy scale buildup. These systems require a stronger commercial solvent available from local distributors. chunk_text:
E-COOLANT-CLEAN-042 冷却系统清洗要求
The carbon dioxide bubbles that form when limescale deposits are dissolved can prevent the cleaning agent from reaching boiler scale. It is therefore abso- lutely necessary to circulate the water with the cleaning agent to flush away the gas bubbles and allow them to escape. The length of the cleaning pro- cess depends on the thickness and composition of the deposits. Values are provided for orientation in the table entitled Cleaning agents for removing limescale and rust deposits, Page 287. Following cleaning The cooling system must be flushed several times once it has been cleaned using cleaning agents. Replace the water during this process. If acids are used to carry out the cleaning, neutralise the cooling system afterwards with suitable chemicals then flush. The system can then be refilled with water that has been prepared accordingly.

chunk_text:
E-PUMP-CLEAN-020 冷却系统清洗要求
Lime and rust deposits Lime and rust deposits can form if the water is especially hard or if the con- centration of the anticorrosive agent is too low. A thin lime scale layer can be left on the surface as experience has shown that this protects against corro- sion. However, limescale deposits with a thickness of more than 0.5 mm ob- struct the transfer of heat and cause thermal overloading of the components being cooled. Rust that has been flushed out may have an abrasive effect on other parts of the system, such as the sealing elements of the water pumps. Together with the elements that are responsible for water hardness, this forms what is known as ferrous sludge which tends to gather in areas where the flow velo- city is low. position on the shaft. NOTE: When installing a new water pump, put a small amount of oil on the bearings. Do not start or turn over an engine unless the cooling system is filled with coolant. If the water pump is operated in a dry condition, seal failure will result from overheating. NOTE: If a cooling system has been flushed, check the condition of the water pump closely for approximately one week. Many times, a seal failure will result soon after the cooling system has been flushed. This is because the loose rust and scale, which is purged by the cleaning process, goes through the pump seal area. Cylinder Heads Normally, cylinder head repair is needed because of leaks or cracks. A defect in a core plug (freeze plug) in the top deck of the cylinder head can cause a leak. If there is a leak in this area, water spots will be visible in the plug recess.

chunk_text:
E-SYS-CLEAN-005 冷却系统清洗要求
Coolant system cleaning Summary Remove contamination/residue from operating fluid systems, ensure/re-estab- lish operating reliability. Coolant systems containing deposits or contamination prevent effective cool- ing of parts. Contamination and deposits must be regularly eliminated. This comprises the following: Cleaning the system and, if required, removal of limescale deposits, flushing the system. Cleaning The coolant system must be checked for contamination at regular intervals. Cleaning is required if the degree of contamination is high. This work should ideally be carried out by a specialist who can provide the right cleaning agents for the type of deposits and materials in the cooling circuit. The cleaning should only be carried out by the engine operator if this cannot be done by a specialist.

8.3 Engine coolant circuits – Flushing 1. Drain engine coolant. 2. Measure pH-value of the fresh water using the MTU test kit or electric pH-value measuring device. 3. Fill coolant circuit with fresh water. Important information Never pour cold water into a hot engine! 4. Preheat, start and run engine until warm. 5. Run engine for approx. 30 minutes at increased speed. 6. Take flush-water sample at engine-coolant-sample extraction cock. 7. Shut down engine. 8. Drain flush water. 9. Measure pH value of flush-water sample using the MTU test kit or electric pH value measuring device and compare with the pH value of the fresh water. a) pH value difference < 1: Fill system with treated coolant and start engine. b) pH value difference > 1: Fill system with fresh flush water and repeat flushing process.

8.4 Engine coolant circuits – Cleaning 1. Mix cleaner to the specified concentration with freshwater. Use warm freshwater (45 °C) if the engine is warm. 2. Cooling water systems containing deposits or contamination prevent effec- tive cooling of parts. Contamination and deposits must be regularly elimina- ted. This comprises the following: Cleaning the system and, if required, removal of limescale deposits, flushing the system. Cleaning The cooling water system must be checked for contamination at regular intervals. Cleaning is required if the degree of contamination is high. This work should ideally be carried out by a specialist who can provide the right cleaning agents for the type of deposits and materials in the cooling circuit. The cleaning should only be carried out by the engine operator if this cannot be done by a specialist. Oil sludge from lubricating oil that has entered the cooling system or a high concentration of anticorrosive agents can be removed by flushing the system

E-SW-CLEAN-006 冷却系统清洗要求
voltage that exists between the two dissimilar metals allows current to flow. Galvanic corrosion occurs on the least resistant metal. In marine applications where sea water is highly conductive, sacrificial material (rods) are placed in seawater flow passages to absorb current flow. Typically, this wear material is either magnesium or zinc. Rods must be inspected regularly and replaced when necessary. Caterpillar recommends inspecting rods every 50 hours until a wear rate is established. In truck, earthmoving, and other non-marine applications, if galvanic corrosion occurs, immediately drain, flush, and refill the coolant mixture. The source of voltage must be determined to prevent continued corrosion. Corrosion can also occur when the source of current flow through the coolant is external.

are running or with a built-in pre-heater. If the engine normally runs on HFO, pre-heated fuel must be circulated through the injection pumps while pre-heating the engine, although the engine just has run or has been flushed on MDO/MGO for a short period. Starting on MDO/MGO For starting on MDO/MGO, there are no restrictions except lubricating oil vis- cosity may not by higher than 1500 cSt. (5°C for SAE 30 or 10°C for SAE 40). Initial ignition may be difficult if the engine and the ambient temperature are lower than 5°C and the cooling water temperature is lower than 15°C. Prelubricating The engine shall always be pre-lubricated 2 minutes prior to start if there is no pre-lubrication at intervals or continuous pre-lubrication installed. Pre-lubrication at intervals is 2 minutes every 10 minutes.

chunk_text:
E-SYS-CLEAN-020 发动机启动与冷却水预热条件
General The engine may be started and loaded according to the following procedure: A: Normal start without preheated cooling water. Only on MDO. B: Normal start with preheated cooling water. MDO or HFO. C: Stand-by engine. Emergency start, with pre- heated cooling water, intermediate prelubri- cating or continuos prelubricating. MDO or HFO. Starting on HFO During shorter stops or if the engine is in stand-by on HFO the engine must be preheated. During preheating the cooling water outlet tempera- ture should be kept as high as possible at least 60°C (± 5°C) -either by means of cooling water from engines which are running or by means of a built-in preheater. If the engine normally runs on HFO preheated fuel must be circulated through the engine while pre- heating although the engine has run or has been flushed on MDO for a short period.

chunk_text:
E-SYS-CTRL-001 冷却液生物污染控制
8.6 Coolant circuits contaminated with bacteria, fungi or yeast System cleaning The system cleaner must flow a sufficiently long time through the complete cooling system to ensure effec- tive cleaning and disinfection. Therefore, the predefined amount of the approved system cleaner must be added to the contaminated cool- ant in the system, see (→ Page 48). Use a circulating pump to provide continuous mixture flow through the coolant system for at least 24 hours or max. 48 hours. Flushing When the coolant and system cleaner have been drained, the cooling circuit must be flushed with fresh wa- ter. Flushing must be carried out until no more contaminants are visible and the flushing liquid has the same pH-value as the fresh water used (max. pH-value difference < 1). Refill Before refilling the circuit, make sure the system is free of contaminants.

E-PIPE-CTRL-007 冷却液生物污染控制
tain chloride or sulphate ions are not permitted. ▪ Biocides that cause foaming of coolant are not permitted. Prerequisite for effective use of an anticorrosive agent Clean cooling system As contamination significantly reduces the effectiveness of the additive, the tanks, pipes, coolers and other parts outside the engine must be free of rust and other deposits before the engine is started up for the first time and after repairs of the pipe system. The entire system must therefore be cleaned with the engine switched off using a suitable cleaning agent (see 010.005 Engine – Work Instructions 010.000.001-01 and 010.000.002-04). Loose solid matter in particular must be removed by flushing the system thoroughly as otherwise erosion may occur in locations where the flow veloc- ity is high.

13.1.3 Pressure Tests Turbine casings are to be subjected to pressure test of 1.5 times the highest pressure in the casing during normal operation. Turbine casings may be divided by temporary diaphragms to allow for an even distribution of the test pressures. Where hydrostatic tests are not practicable, alternative tests to determine soundness and workmanship are to be submitted for consideration and approval in each case. Intercoolers and heat exchangers are to be hydrostatically tested on both sides to 1.5 times the design pressure.

E-HT-COMP-090 高温冷却水系统组成
0.01666 (hr/min) Some technical data sheets list the Heat Input with the Heat Balance Data under the name “Fuel Input” or “LHV Input”. Work Output (W) The work output is the shaft power created from the engine. It is the power that the engine generates from the fuel and is the total of the flywheel power and any driven equipment. Driven equipment includes alternators, equipment driven off the accessory drives and equipment on the front stub shaft such as a radiator fan. The power used internal to the engine is included in the heat load values. These include the jacket water pump, aftercooler pump, friction and gear train loads. Work Output is expressed in bkW or bhp. To convert between units of horsepower and kW, use the factor: 1hp = 0.7457 kW. To convert bhp to Btu/min, use the factor: 1hp = 42.42 Btu/min.

E-COOLER-DRAW-001 中央冷却器选型要求
Design features and working principle This diagram describes the possibilities with regard to the design of a com- mon auxiliary system for a two-stroke main engine of the MC-type and four- stroke GenSets fromMAN Energy Solutions. The central cooling system is an alternative to the conventional seawater cool- ing system, based on the same design principles with regard to cooler loca- tions, flow control and preheating, but with a central cooler and one additional set of pumps. The central cooler minimizes maintenance work by being the only component that is in contact with seawater. In all other parts of the sys- tem, inhibited fresh water is used in accordance with MAN Energy Solutions' specifications. Operation at sea The seawater cooling pumps, item 1, pump seawater from the sea chests through the central cooler, item 2, and overboard.

chunk_text:
E-SYS-DRAW-001 外部冷却水系统设计原则
Ad 1) Cooling water systems have a tendency to be unnecessarily complicated and thus uneconomic in installation and operation. Therfore, we have attached great importance to simple diagram design with optimal cooling of the engines and at the same time installation- and operation-friendly systems resulting in economic advantages. Ad 2) It has been stressed on the diagrams that the alternator engines in stand- by position as well as the propulsion engine in stop position are preheated, op- timally and simply, with surplus heat from the running engines. Ad 3) If the engines are preheated with reverse cooling water direction, i.e. from the top and downwards, an optimal heat distribution is reached in the engine. This method is at the same time more economic since the need for heating is less and the water flow is reduced.

Cooling of the nozzle cooling water is effected by the LT cooling water.

E-PUMP-DRAW-002 中央冷却器选型要求
Design features and working principle This diagram describes the possibilities with regard to the design of a com- mon auxiliary system for a two-stroke main engine of the MC-type and four- stroke GenSets fromMAN Energy Solutions. The central cooling system is an alternative to the conventional seawater cool- ing system, based on the same design principles with regard to cooler loca- tions, flow control and preheating, but with a central cooler and one additional set of pumps. The central cooler minimizes maintenance work by being the only component that is in contact with seawater. In all other parts of the sys- tem, inhibited fresh water is used in accordance with MAN Energy Solutions' specifications. Operation at sea The seawater cooling pumps, item 1, pump seawater from the sea chests through the central cooler, item 2, and overboard.

In case of one-string cooling water system are the dual fuel engine is delivered with connection branches for the external preheater unit. chunk_text:
E-VALVE-DRAW-001 外部冷却水系统设计原则
External cooling water system Design of external cooling water system It is not difficult to make a system fulfil the requirements, but to make the sys- tem both simple and cheap and still fulfil the requirements of both the engine builder and other parties involved can be very difficult. A simple version cannot be made without involving the engine builder. The diagrams on the following pages are principal diagrams, and are MAN Energy Solutions' recommendation for the design of external cooling water systems. The systems are designed on the basis of the following criteria: 1. Simplicity 2. Separate HT temperature regulation for propulsion and alternator engines. 3. HT temperature regulation on engine outlet. 4. Preheating with surplus heat. 5. Preheating in engine top, downwards. 6. As few change-over valves as possible. 7. Possibility for MAN Energy Solutions ICS-system.

Possibility for MAN Diesel & Turbo ICS-system.

The systems are designed on the basis of the following criteria: 1. Simplicity. 2. Preheating with surplus heat. 3. Preheating in engine top, downwards. 4. As few change-over valves as possible.

Design features and working principle This diagram describes the possibilities with regard to the design of a com- mon auxiliary system for a two-stroke main engine of the MC-type and four- stroke GenSets from MAN Energy Solutions. The jacket water cooling system controls the temperature of the engines proper. The jacket water is to be inhibited to protect the surfaces of the cooling sys- tem against corrosion, corrosion fatigue, cavitation and the formation of scale. Operation at sea The jacket water pumps circulate hot cooling water from the engines to the fresh water generator and from there to the jacket water cooler. Here a ther- mostatically controlled 3-way valve mixes cooled and uncooled water to main- tain an outlet temperature of 80-82°C from the main engine.

Service Ports Service ports can be found on the Engine Installation Drawings, published in EDDC. Ports on Jacket Water (JW) Heat Exchanger  Sea Water Drains  Treated Water Drain Port on Aftercooler SCAC Heat Exchanger  Treated Water Drain Water Quality, Rust Inhibitors, and Antifreeze Maintaining water quality is very important in closed cooling systems. Excessive hardness will cause deposits, fouling, and reduced effectiveness of cooling system components. Caterpillar has coolant inhibitor available to properly condition the cooling water. When using Cat inhibitor, the cooling water piping must not be a galvanized material, and aluminum should not be used. If the piping is galvanized, the zinc will react with the coolant inhibitor causing material to deposits in the treated water system which may lead to fouling in the treated water circuit.

combustion and at the same time cold corrosion is avoided; the latter is also the reason why the engine, in stand-by position and when starting on HFO, should be preheated with a cooling water temperature of ≥ 60°C – either by means of cooling water from running engines or by means of a separate pre- heating system. System lay-out MAN Diesel's standard for the internal cooling water system is shown on our Basic Diagram. This means that it is only nessesary with two main pipes for cooling of the engine. The only demand is that the FW inlet temperature is between 10 and 40°C. chunk_text:
E-SYS-DRAW-021 冷却水温度与压力参数
An engine outlet temperature of 80°C ensures a perfect combustion in the en- tire load area when running on Heavy Fuel Oil (HFO), i.e. this temperature lim- its the thermal loads in the high-load area, and hot corrosion in the combus- tion area is avoided. In the low-load area, the temperature is sufficiently high to secure a perfect combustion and at the same time cold corrosion is avoided; the latter is also the reason why the engine, in stand-by position and when starting on HFO, should be preheated with a medium cooling water temperature of ≥ 60°C – either by means of cooling water from running engines or by means of a sep- arate preheating system. System lay-out MAN Energy Solutions' standard for the internal cooling water system is shown on Basis Diagram 2. The system has been constructed with a view to full integration into the external system.

E-TCV-DRAW-004 温度控制阀配置
From here, it is pumped through a manifold into the nozzle cooling water ser- vice tank from where it returns to the pump. One system can be installed for up to three engines. T-076/Nozzle cooling water service tank The nozzle cooling water service tank (T-076) is used for deaeration of the nozzle cooling water. HE-005/Nozzle cooling wa- ter cooler The nozzle cooling water cooler is to be connected in the LT cooling water cir- cuit according to schematic diagram. Cooling of the nozzle cooling water is effected by the LT cooling water. If an antifreeze is added to the cooling water, the resulting lower heat transfer rate must be taken into consideration. The cooler is to be provided with vent- ing and draining facilities. TCV-005/Nozzle cooling water temperature control valve The nozzle cooling water temperature control valve with thermal-expansion

E-EXP-DRAW-009 温度控制阀配置
9.3.8 Waste heat recovery The waste heat in the HT cooling water can be used for fresh water production, central heating, tank heating etc. The system should in such case be provided with a temperature control valve to avoid unnecessary cooling, as shown in the example diagrams. With this arrangement the HT water flow through the heat re- covery can be increased. The heat available from HT cooling water is affected by ambient conditions. It should also be taken into account that the recoverable heat is reduced by circulation to the expansion tank, radiation from piping and leakages in temperature control valves.

E-CENTRAL-DRAW-001 海水侧系统组成
Central Cooling Systems A central cooling system is defined as one which cools multiple engines and which combines many individual cooling system components (heat exchangers and pumps) into a large central one. However, there are both advantages and disadvantages to a central cooling system that must be considered when making that determination. A typical marine central cooling system diagram is shown in Figure 64. Advantages of a Central Cooling System • A central cooling system will reduce the extent of the seawater piping system and thereby reduce wear, corrosion, and maintenance. • The reduced extent of the seawater system will also significantly reduce the amount of shipyard labor required to install such a system.

chunk_text:
E-HT-DRAW-008 高温冷却水系统组成
The high temperature cooling water is used for the cooling of cylinder liners and cylinder heads. An engine outlet temperature of 80°C ensures a perfect combustion in the entire load area when running on Heavy Fuel Oil (HFO), i.e. this tempera- ture limits the thermal loads in the high-load area, and hot corrosion in the combustion area is avoi- ded. In the low-load area, the temperature is sufficiently high to secure a perfect combustion and at the same time cold corrosion is avoided; the latter is also the reason why the engine, in stand-by position and when starting on HFO, should be preheated with a medium cooling water temperature of ≥ 60°C – either by means of cooling water from running engines or by means of a separate preheating sys- tem. System lay-out MAN Diesel & Turbo's standard for the internal cooling water system is shown on Basis Diagram 2.

针对船舶中央冷却系统淡水侧向各冷却支管输送淡水时，实际流量与设计流量会有较大差别的问题，以4台冷却设备为例构建淡水侧计算模型，从简单管路的流量、阻抗等特性出发，提出阻抗平衡计算方法，采用实际算例对计算步骤进行演示，并利用Flowmaster软件对算例进行仿真，仿真结果与理论计算结果吻合良好，验证了阻抗平衡法计算的正确性，最后采用阻抗平衡法反向计算出了设计流量下的各支管阻抗以及局部阻力系数。结论表明，阻抗平衡法能准确进行管路水力计算，在船舶中央冷却系统设计过程中可进行实际应用。

In view of the problem that the actual flow and the design flow will be greatly different when the central cooling system delivers fresh water to each cooling branch, taking four cooling equipments as examples, the calculation model of fresh water side is constructed. Based on the flow, impedance and other characteristics of the simple pipeline, the impedance balance calculation method is proposed, and the calculation steps are demonstrated with an actual example. The example is simulated with Flowmaster. The simulation results are in good agreement with the theoretical calculation results, which verifies the correctness of the impedance balance calculation method. Finally, impedance balance method is used to calculate the impedance and local resistance coefficient of each branch pipe under the design flow. S03 《全船技术规格书》GCY847-020-002SM

E-SYS-FLOW-014 淡水侧流向
Engine Price List. Contact Caterpillar for more details on these cooling systems. Compressor Oil Coolers A compressor oil cooler (or other external heat load) should be connected into the aftercooler circuit after the water has left the aftercooler. The return line back into the circuit should be placed before the thermostat. If full flow is not needed to the compressor oil cooler, a bypass line along with any necessary valves can be installed in parallel with the compressor oil cooler. The additional heat load into to the aftercooler circuit needs to be included when sizing the radiator. The additional restriction of the compressor oil cooler and bypass must be included in the circuit's external restriction calculations. The total circuit restriction must not exceed the maximum allowable external restriction. The flow to the aftercooler is critical in gas engines.

主机冷却水泵数量与容量要求（IACS UR M3.1）
IACS Unified Requirements M3.1 — Cooling Systems
At least two independent cooling water pumps shall be fitted for the cooling of main propulsion machinery. Where engine-driven pumps are fitted, at least one independently driven pump shall be provided. Each pump shall have sufficient capacity to supply the full cooling water flow required by the main engine under maximum continuous rating (MCR) conditions. The pumps shall be capable of being started independently and the changeover shall be achievable without interrupting operation.
整理说明：IACS UR M3.1 为主机冷却水泵数量、独立驱动要求及泵容量提供了规范级依据。可支撑冷却水泵冗余配置、容量设计及换泵操作类需求。

主机冷却水温度监控与报警要求（IACS UR M3.1）
IACS Unified Requirements M3.1 — Temperature Monitoring and Alarm
Cooling water temperature of main propulsion engines shall be continuously monitored. High temperature alarms shall be set not to exceed the engine manufacturer's maximum permissible cooling water temperature. Where automatic slow-down or shutdown is fitted, the activation set-point shall be above the alarm set-point and shall not exceed the manufacturer's absolute maximum cooling water temperature limit.
整理说明：IACS UR M3.1 对主机冷却水温度监控、报警设定及自动降速/停机要求提供了规范级依据。可支撑温度监控、报警阈值及自动保护类需求。

冷却水泵容量余量与中央冷却系统容量要求（IACS UR M3.1）
IACS Unified Requirements M3.1 — Cooling Water System Capacity Margin
The total installed cooling water pump capacity shall provide a minimum margin of 25% above the maximum calculated system flow demand. For central cooling systems, the low-temperature (LT) freshwater circuit shall have sufficient capacity to handle the combined heat rejection of all connected consumers simultaneously at their maximum loads, including at the maximum anticipated seawater temperature for the vessel's intended trading area.
整理说明：IACS UR M3.1 要求总冷却水泵容量应比最大计算流量需求高出25%的余量，中央冷却系统低温回路需满足所有连接设备在最高海水温度下同时满负荷运行的需求。

主机冷却水系统温度设计要求（DNV规则）
DNV Rules for Classification: Ships, Pt.4 Ch.3 — Cooling Water Systems
The cooling water system for main propulsion engines shall be designed so that the cooling water temperatures at the engine inlet are maintained within the limits specified by the engine manufacturer. For high-temperature (HT) fresh water circuits, the maximum inlet temperature to the engine shall not exceed 36°C above the thermostat opening temperature under worst-case ambient conditions. For central (low-temperature) cooling systems, the LT fresh water temperature at the plate cooler outlet shall be calculated for maximum sea water temperature at the service area.
整理说明：DNV船级社规则对主机冷却水进机温度范围、温控阀调节范围及中央冷却系统低温回路设计提供了规范级依据。可支撑温度参数限制、系统设计及温控阀配置类需求。

主机冷却水泵冗余配置与自动切换要求（DNV规则）
DNV Rules for Classification: Ships, Pt.4 Ch.3 — Cooling Water Pump Redundancy
At least two cooling water pumps shall be provided for the main engine cooling circuit. The pumps shall be arranged so that failure of one pump does not prevent the operation of the remaining pump(s). Where one pump is engine-driven, the other shall be electrically driven. Each pump shall be capable of maintaining required cooling water flow at all engine load conditions from idle to MCR. Automatic changeover to the standby pump shall be provided in case of pump failure, with alarm indication.

DNV Rules for Classification: Ships, Pt.4 Ch.3 — Sea Trial Requirements for Cooling Systems
During sea trials, the cooling water system shall be tested to demonstrate:
1. Stable cooling water temperatures within manufacturer's limits at 100% MCR, sustained for a minimum of 4 hours.
2. Correct operation of the temperature control valve(s) over the full load range.

主机冷却水系统配置要求（CCS规则）
中国船级社（CCS）钢质海船入级规范 第4篇 第3章 — 冷却水系统
主推进机械的冷却水系统应设有不少于2台冷却水泵，其中至少1台应为独立电力驱动。各泵应具有在主机额定功率工况下单独满足冷却水流量需求的能力。系统应设置冷却水高温报警，报警值应不超过主机制造商规定的最高允许温度。当冷却水温度超过允许值时，应能自动减速或停机保护。
冷却水系统的设计应能在主机最大连续功率（MCR）条件下，在航行海区最高海水温度（不低于32°C）时保持正常工作，热带航区应不低于35°C。
整理说明：CCS规则对主机冷却水系统泵配置、报警和系统设计提供了中国船级社规范级依据，可支撑国内船厂建造项目的合规性要求。

冷却水系统安装后试验和海试要求（CCS规则）
中国船级社（CCS）钢质海船入级规范 第4篇 第3章 — 冷却水系统试验
冷却水系统在安装完成后应进行以下试验：
1. 管路水压试验：各管路应按设计压力的1.5倍进行水压试验，保压时间不少于30分钟，不得有渗漏现象。
2. 功能试验：所有冷却水泵、阀件、温控阀、膨胀水箱液位报警及冷却水高温报警等应逐项进行功能试验。
3. 系泊试验：主机在码头试验工况下，验证冷却水系统的基本功能和报警设定值。
4. 航行试验：主机在MCR工况下持续运行，验证冷却水系统在各负荷下的稳定性和各报警设定值的正确性。
整理说明：CCS规则对冷却水系统安装后试验、系泊试验和航行试验提供了系统性规范要求，可支撑冷却水管路试压、功能验证及海试验收类需求。

主推进机械冷却系统冗余与报警要求（SOLAS Reg.26）
SOLAS 2020 Consolidated Edition, Chapter II-1, Part C, Regulation 26 — Machinery: Cooling
26.1 Adequate means of cooling shall be provided for the main propulsion machinery and for all machinery essential for the propulsion and safety of the ship.
26.2 The cooling systems shall be arranged to ensure continued cooling of the main engine in the event of failure of the primary cooling water pump, either by provision of a standby pump with automatic start capability or by other approved means.
26.3 Suitable means shall be provided to detect the failure of cooling, by alarms giving warning of abnormal temperatures in the cooling system.

chunk_text:
主机冷却水系统调试与海试程序（综合规范实践）
Marine Diesel Engine Cooling Water System — Commissioning and Sea Trial Procedure
(Consolidated from IACS UR M3.1, DNV Rules Pt.4 Ch.3, and standard shipyard practice)

Pre-sea trial checks:
1. Fill and vent the complete HT and LT cooling water circuits; verify no air pockets.
2. Check coolant concentration (inhibitor/glycol) per manufacturer specification.
3. Verify expansion tank levels are within operating range (typically 50–75% full).
4. Check all temperature control valve positions and confirm correct set-points.
5. Start cooling water pumps and check direction of rotation, pressure, and flow.
6. Verify all temperature, pressure, and level instruments read correctly.

Sea trial test sequence:
1. Run engine at 25%, 50%, 75%, and 100% MCR — record HT/LT temperatures and pressures.
2. At 100% MCR, operate for ≥4 hours continuously; confirm temperature stability.
3. Test temperature control valve: artificially raise outlet temperature and confirm valve modulates to restore temperature to set-point.
4. Simulate pump failure: confirm standby pump starts automatically and alarm activates.
5. Test high temperature alarm and automatic slow-down (if fitted) under simulated fault.
6. Confirm expansion tank low-level alarm activates at set water level.

Acceptance criteria:
- HT water temperature at engine inlet: within manufacturer's stated range.
- LT water temperature: below maximum specified for connected auxiliaries.
- All alarms and automatic functions operate correctly.
整理说明：本程序综合IACS UR M3.1、DNV规则和标准船厂实践，为冷却水系统试车和海试提供了系统性的试验流程和验收标准，可支撑试验类需求的内容和接受准则。

中央冷却系统低温回路容量设计要求（DNV规则）
DNV Rules for Classification: Ships, Pt.4 Ch.3 — Central Cooling System Design
Low-Temperature (LT) Freshwater Cooling Circuit Capacity Requirements:
The LT freshwater circuit of a central cooling system shall be sized to handle the combined heat rejection from all consumers connected to the LT circuit, operating simultaneously at their maximum rated loads. The sizing calculation shall be performed for the maximum seawater temperature of the vessel's intended trading area (minimum 32°C for unrestricted service, 35°C for tropical service).
The flow rate through the central freshwater cooler shall be adequate to limit the LT water temperature rise across the cooler to the value required to maintain all connected consumers within their temperature limits.
典型LT冷却水进中央冷却器温度：30–40°C；出中央冷却器温度：32–38°C（取决于海水温度）。

chunk_text:
主机冷却水温度控制系统功能要求（IACS UR E10）
IACS Unified Requirements E10 — Machinery Control Systems
Cooling water temperature control systems for main propulsion engines shall:
1. Maintain cooling water temperature within manufacturer's limits across the full engine load range through automatic modulation of the temperature control valve.
2. Be capable of manual override in case of automatic control failure.
3. Provide alarm when cooling water temperature exceeds the high alarm set-point.
4. Where automatic slow-down or shutdown is provided, activate at a set-point above the alarm set-point (typically 5–10°C above the alarm).
5. Activate an audible and visible alarm when automatic protective devices are triggered.
6. Maintain cooling water temperature control function after a single failure of any control system component (single-failure criterion).
整理说明：IACS UR E10 对主机冷却水温度控制系统的功能要求、手动备用、自动保护逻辑和单一故障准则提供了规范级依据，可支撑控制系统设计、保护逻辑和可靠性类需求。

冷却水系统UMS监控参数清单（IACS UR E10）
IACS Unified Requirements E10 — Cooling Water System Monitoring Requirements
The following monitoring parameters are required for unattended machinery spaces (UMS) certification. For manned machinery spaces, these are recommended best practice:
- HT cooling water temperature at engine outlet: continuous monitoring, high alarm
- HT cooling water pressure at engine inlet: continuous monitoring, low alarm
- LT cooling water temperature at central cooler outlet: continuous monitoring, high alarm
- Expansion tank level: monitoring, low level alarm
- Cooling water pump running status: indication
- Temperature control valve position: indication (recommended)
All alarms shall be connected to the alarm management system and indicated at the machinery control console and the bridge.
整理说明：IACS UR E10 为无人值守机舱（UMS）认证规定了冷却水系统监控参数清单，为控制系统的监测功能设计提供了规范级依据。

chunk_text:
膨胀水箱容量与安装要求（DNV规则）
DNV Rules for Classification: Ships, Pt.4 Ch.3 — Expansion Tank Requirements
The expansion tank for the freshwater cooling circuit shall:
1. Have sufficient capacity to accommodate the volume expansion of the cooling water from cold (ambient) to maximum operating temperature, plus a reserve volume. Minimum tank volume: at least 5% of the total cooling water volume in the circuit, or as specified by the engine manufacturer, whichever is greater.
2. Be located at the highest point of the cooling water circuit to allow venting.
3. Be fitted with a level gauge, low-level alarm, and filling connection.
4. Be connected to the cooling circuit by a pipe that allows free expansion and venting without significant flow restriction.
5. Not be pressurised unless specifically designed as a pressurised expansion vessel.

主机HT/LT冷却水系统标准参数范围（综合IACS/ISO/DNV）
Marine Main Engine HT Cooling Water System — Standard Parameter Limits
(Consolidated from IACS UR M3.1, ISO 8861, DNV Rules, and engine manufacturer project guides for medium-speed 4-stroke diesel engines)

High-Temperature (HT) Freshwater Circuit:
- Engine jacket water inlet temperature: 70–85°C (exact value per manufacturer)
- Engine jacket water outlet temperature: 80–95°C (exact value per manufacturer)
- Temperature control valve set-point (thermostat): typically 80–85°C
- High temperature alarm: 90–95°C (5–10°C above set-point, per manufacturer)
- Automatic slow-down activation: 95–100°C (per manufacturer, above alarm)
- Maximum cooling water pressure: as specified by manufacturer (typically 3–5 bar)
- Minimum cooling water pressure at engine inlet: typically 1.5–3.0 bar
- Low pressure alarm: 0.5–1.0 bar below minimum operating pressure

Low-Temperature (LT) Freshwater Circuit (Central Cooling):
- LT water temperature at central cooler outlet: 25–38°C (depends on seawater temperature)
- LT water temperature at central cooler inlet: 35–45°C
- High temperature alarm for LT water: 5°C above maximum design temperature

IACS Unified Requirements M72 — Hydraulic Testing of Cooling-System Components
(Directly extracted from IACS UR M72, verified via ClassNK TEC-1066)

Hydraulic testing requirements for cooling water components:
- All items in contact with cooling water are to be tested by hydraulic pressure at a pressure equal to 1.5 times the maximum working pressure (M72 Footnote 3, directly extracted).
- Hydraulic testing is required for those parts filled with cooling water and having the function of containing the water which is in contact with the cylinder or cylinder liner (M72 Footnote 9, directly extracted).
- Component certification: For engines with bore D > 300 mm, coolers (both sides, including charge air cooler water side) require a Work Certificate (W).
- Engine-driven pumps (oil, water, fuel, bilge) require Work Certificate (W) for engines > 800 kW/cylinder.

柴油机分级认证标准环境参考条件（IACS UR M28）
IACS Unified Requirements M28 — Standard Ambient Reference Conditions
(Verified via multiple IACS-aligned sources and M73 cross-reference)

Standard design ambient conditions for diesel engine classification and certification:
- Air blower/turbocharger inlet temperature: 45°C
- Air blower inlet pressure: 1,000 mbar (1.0 bar absolute)
- Seawater temperature (at cooler inlet): 32°C
- Relative humidity: 60%

Application: These are the reference conditions against which engine MCR performance is rated. The seawater temperature of 32°C is the baseline for all cooling system capacity calculations for unrestricted service. For tropical service areas, the design seawater temperature shall be 35°C.

Note: IACS UR M73.3.1.1 (directly extracted) confirms turbocharger component lifetime must be based on 45°C air inlet temperature, consistent with M28.

chunk_text:
冷却水系统在船舶倾斜工况下的工作要求（SOLAS Reg.26，直接摘录）
SOLAS Chapter II-1, Regulation 26.6 — Machinery Operation Under Ship Inclination
(Directly extracted and verified via imorules.com)

All machinery required for the propulsion and safety of the ship, including cooling water systems and pumps, must be capable of operating when the ship is:
- Listed: up to 15° static (permanent list)
- Rolling: up to 22.5° dynamic (transient)
- Pitching: up to 7.5°

Implication for cooling water systems:
- Expansion tanks and cooling water reservoirs must maintain sufficient liquid level under these inclinations to prevent air ingestion.
- Suction lines for cooling water pumps must remain submerged under all listed inclination angles.
- Expansion tank sizing must account for the volume shift under 15° list.

Dead ship condition (SOLAS Reg. 26, para. 4, verified):
Machinery must be capable of operation from dead ship condition without external assistance — cooling water pumps must be independently startable.

整理说明：SOLAS Reg. 26.6（经imorules.com验证）规定船舶冷却水系统必须在15°横倾、22.5°横摇、7.5°纵摇条件下正常工作，并能从机舱黑船状态自主启动，为膨胀水箱容量和泵吸口设计提供了法规级依据。

冷却系统设计要求与换热器容量余量（ISO 8861:1998）
ISO 8861:1998 Shipbuilding and Marine Structures — Main and Auxiliary Machinery — Requirements for Cooling Systems
Section 5 — General Design Requirements:
The cooling system shall be designed to maintain cooling water temperatures within the limits specified by the machinery manufacturer(s) under all operating conditions, including maximum continuous rating (MCR) and maximum anticipated ambient seawater temperature.
Section 6 — Cooling Capacity:
The net cooling capacity of the heat exchangers (sea water coolers or central cooler) shall be sufficient to remove the total heat rejection from all connected machinery operating simultaneously at MCR, with an additional safety margin of at least 15% to account for fouling and ageing of the heat exchanger surfaces.
整理说明：ISO 8861:1998 为船舶主辅机冷却系统设计提供了国际标准依据，覆盖设计温度范围和换热器净冷却能力余量要求，是容量设计和参数确认的权威标准参考。

冷却水系统监测与报警参数要求（ISO 8861:1998）
ISO 8861:1998 Shipbuilding and Marine Structures — Cooling System Monitoring Requirements
Section 8 — Monitoring and Alarm:
The following parameters shall be monitored and alarmed for main engine cooling water systems:
a) High temperature of HT cooling water at engine outlet: alarm set-point to be within manufacturer's limits (typically 85–95°C for large 4-stroke engines);
b) Low pressure of cooling water at engine inlet: alarm set-point as specified by manufacturer;
c) Low level in expansion tank: alarm when level falls below minimum operating level;
d) High temperature of LT cooling water: alarm set-point as per central cooler design.
All alarms shall be indicated in the engine control room and navigating bridge.
整理说明：ISO 8861:1998 规定了主机冷却水系统的监测参数、报警设定和报警位置，为冷却水监测、报警配置和控制系统设计提供了国际标准依据。

chunk_text:
海水冷却系统过滤器配置要求（双联/反冲洗）
Marine Cooling System — Sea Chest Strainer Configuration Requirements
(Based on DNV Rules for Classification Pt.4 Ch.3, IACS UR M3, and standard class practice)

Sea water cooling systems shall be provided with effective strainers on all sea water suction lines upstream of cooling pumps and heat exchangers:
1. Duplex (twin) strainers with in-line changeover shall be fitted on sea water suction lines serving essential cooling machinery, allowing one strainer to be cleaned while the other remains in service without interrupting cooling water flow.
2. Strainer basket mesh size: typically 0.8–2.0 mm clear opening, appropriate to protect downstream equipment.
3. Each strainer shall be fitted with a pressure differential indicator or alarm; high differential pressure alarm set-point shall be defined in the system design.
4. Where automatic self-cleaning (backwash) strainers are fitted, the backwash mechanism shall operate without interrupting cooling water flow, and shall be capable of automatic initiation on high differential pressure signal.
5. Strainer bodies shall be rated for full system design pressure and tested to 1.5× design pressure before installation.
整理说明：海水冷却系统过滤器配置规范：双联切换过滤器（不停机清洗）、网孔0.8–2.0mm、压差报警、自动反冲洗功能（高压差自动触发）、壳体1.5倍设计压力试验。

海水冷却系统双联过滤器及反冲洗要求（CCS规则）
中国船级社（CCS）钢质海船入级规范 — 海水冷却系统过滤器规范要求

1. 冷却主机等重要设备的海水进水管路应设置双联过滤器（备用切换），以便在不停机条件下清洗维护，保证系统连续运行能力。
2. 过滤器应安装在冷却水泵进口前，进出口间应设置压差指示装置；当压差超过设定值时应发出报警，提示操作人员清洗或切换过滤器。
3. 在热带海域和海生物附着高风险航区长期运营的船舶，宜配置具有自动反冲洗功能的过滤器，以减少人工清洗频次，防止冷却水流量不足。
4. 过滤器壳体及管路连接件应按1.5倍最高工作压力进行水压试验，保压时间不少于30分钟，不得有渗漏现象。
5. 过滤网目数应根据下游设备（泵、热交换器）的保护需求选定，不得在海试期间未经检查就关闭压差报警信号。
整理说明：CCS规则对海水冷却系统双联过滤器配置、在线切换清洗能力、压差报警、热带航区自动反冲洗功能及壳体水压试验提供了规范依据。

chunk_text:
冷却水系统设备维护通道间距要求（DNV/IACS）
Marine Machinery Installation — Maintenance Access and Clearance Requirements
(Based on DNV Rules for Classification: Ships, Pt.4 Ch.1, IACS UR M3, ISO 14122-3, and standard marine engineering practice)

Maintenance and accessibility requirements for cooling water system components:
1. All major cooling water equipment (pumps, heat exchangers, temperature control valves, strainers) shall have sufficient clearance for routine maintenance and component removal without disturbing adjacent equipment.
2. Recommended minimum clearances:
   - Pump: axial clearance ≥ 1.5× pump casing length for impeller/shaft removal; radial clearance ≥ shaft diameter + 100 mm
   - Plate heat exchanger / tube bundle: full plate/tube bundle pull-out length on one side
   - Valve handwheel/actuator: minimum 600 mm operating side clearance
3. Walkway minimum clear width: 600 mm where personnel pass through; 500 mm where inspection only
4. Overhead lifting provisions (pad eye or monorail) shall be provided for equipment with removal mass > 25 kg
5. All equipment requiring periodic maintenance shall have clear nameplates with maintenance interval and tag number
整理说明：冷却水系统设备维护间距要求（DNV/IACS/ISO 14122-3）：泵轴向间距≥1.5倍泵长，板式换热器需留全板束抽出空间；通道宽度≥600mm；>25kg设备须有吊装点；设备须有维护标牌。

冷却水系统模块化快拆设计要求
Marine Engineering Best Practice — Modular Design and Quick-Exchange Requirements for Cooling System Equipment
(Consolidated from DNV Rules, class society guidance, and international shipbuilding practice)

Design requirements to minimise downtime during maintenance and component exchange:
1. Cooling water pumps: shall be designed for in-situ impeller/mechanical seal replacement without removing the pump casing from the pipeline (back-pull-out design), OR shall have flanged connections permitting removal as a complete unit within the maintenance clearance.
2. Heat exchangers: shall be of removable-bundle or gasketed plate-frame type where practical, allowing cleaning/inspection without full removal from the cooling circuit.
3. Temperature control valves: shall be fitted with upstream and downstream isolating valves, permitting in-situ actuator and trim replacement while maintaining other cooling circuits in service.
4. All equipment shall use standardised flanged or threaded connections compatible with ship-standard pipe dimensions, to permit rapid exchange with equivalent spare units.
5. Spare parts for critical components (pump mechanical seals, TCV actuators, strainer baskets, heat exchanger gaskets) shall be listed in the Class-approved spare parts list with manufacturer part numbers.
整理说明：冷却水系统模块化快拆设计要求：泵采用背抽式设计支持就地更换密封，板式换热器须可拆芯清洗，温控阀两侧须有截止阀支持在线更换，备品配件须入级认可备件清单。

chunk_text:
冷却水管路焊接质量与无损检测要求（IACS UR W7/W28）
IACS Unified Requirements W7 / W28 — Welding Quality Requirements for Marine Cooling Water Piping Systems

Requirements for welding of cooling water pipelines on essential machinery systems:
1. Welder qualification: All butt welds in cooling water piping of essential machinery systems shall be made by welders holding valid certificates to IACS UR W7 or equivalent (ISO 9606-1, ASME IX). Certificates shall cover the applicable material group and joint type.
2. Welding procedure qualification (WPS/PQR): per IACS UR W28 or ISO 15614-1 before production welding commences; WPS records shall be retained for class review.
3. Non-destructive examination (NDE) of completed welds:
   - DN > 100 mm and design pressure > 1.0 MPa: minimum 10% random RT or UT of butt welds
   - Critical locations (expansion loops, penetrations, tee branches): 100% visual + selective PT/MT
   - All completed welds: 100% visual examination per class surveyor's instructions
4. Hydrostatic test: all piping after welding and before insulation, at 1.5× design pressure, hold ≥ 30 min (per IACS UR M72)
5. Weld repairs: defective welds found by NDE shall be repaired and re-examined; results recorded in the welding inspection report submitted to class surveyor.
整理说明：IACS UR W7/W28 对船用冷却水管路焊工资质（ISO 9606-1/ASME IX）、焊接工艺评定、无损检测（DN>100mm高压管路≥10% RT/UT）和水压试验要求提供了规范级依据。

冷却水管路焊接质量与无损检测要求（CCS规范）
中国船级社（CCS）钢质海船入级规范 第5篇 — 管路系统焊接与检验要求

冷却水管路系统建造质量验收要求：
1. 焊工资质：冷却水管路焊工应持有CCS或认可机构签发的有效焊工证书，证书覆盖范围应与所焊接材料类别、接头型式和位置一致。
2. 焊接工艺评定（WPS/WPQR）：生产焊接前按CCS要求完成焊接工艺评定，评定文件经CCS审批，保存备查。
3. 无损检测（NDT）要求：
   - 主机冷却水主管路（公称直径≥80mm，设计压力≥1.0 MPa）：随机抽检RT或UT，比例≥10%
   - 关键部位焊缝（弯头、三通、管道贯穿处附近）：增加MT/PT局部检测
   - 全部焊缝：100%外观检验，不合格焊缝须返修复检
4. 管路水压试验：安装完成后，按设计压力1.5倍进行水压试验，保压时间≥30分钟，不得有渗漏或变形。
5. 记录归档：无损检测报告、水压试验记录、返修记录均须存档并提交CCS验船师审核。
整理说明：CCS规范对冷却水管路焊工资质、工艺评定、无损检测要求（≥10% RT/UT）和水压试验的系统性规定，可支撑管路焊接质量、检验记录和安装验收类需求。

chunk_text:
冷却水泵NPSH汽蚀余量计算与选泵要求（ISO 9906）
ISO 9906:2012 — Rotodynamic Pumps: Hydraulic Performance Acceptance Tests
Applied to Marine Cooling Water Pump NPSH Requirements

NPSH (Net Positive Suction Head) requirements for cooling water pump selection and system design:
1. The available NPSH at the pump suction (NPSHa) shall exceed the pump's required NPSH (NPSHr, from manufacturer's curve at rated flow) by the required safety margin:
   NPSHa ≥ NPSHr + safety margin
   Minimum safety margin: 0.5 m (ISO 9906 acceptance basis);
   Recommended for shipboard cooling pumps: 1.0–2.0 m margin
2. NPSHa calculation at worst-case operating condition:
   NPSHa = (p_static / ρg) + h_static - h_friction - (p_vapour / ρg)
   where: p_static = static system pressure at suction; h_static = liquid head above pump centreline; h_friction = suction pipe friction losses at max flow;
   p_vapour = saturation pressure at maximum coolant temperature
3. Worst-case conditions to evaluate:
   - Maximum cooling water temperature (highest vapour pressure)
   - Minimum liquid level in expansion tank (lowest h_static)
   - Maximum system flow (highest h_friction)
4. For closed HT circuits: the static pressurisation from the expansion tank (typically 0.5–1.5 bar gauge) provides significant positive NPSHa contribution, making cavitation rare if system is properly pressurised.
5. Pump test: ISO 9906 Grade 2 or Grade 1 acceptance test shall confirm NPSHr at rated duty point does not exceed the factory test value.
整理说明：ISO 9906 对冷却水泵NPSH选泵和系统设计要求：NPSHa须超过NPSHr至少0.5m（船用推荐1.0–2.0m）；最不利工况（最高水温+最低液位+最大流量）下校核；密闭HT回路系统加压可有效保证足够NPSHa。

chunk_text:
冷却水系统材料选型要求（海水侧/淡水侧/防腐）
Marine Cooling Water System — Material Selection for Seawater-Exposed Components
(Based on DNV Rules Pt.4 Ch.6, IACS UR, ASTM B111, and ISO 6509)

Material requirements by circuit:

Seawater circuit (sea chests, strainers, seawater pump casings, cooler seawater side, overboard piping):
- ACCEPTABLE: Gunmetal / red brass (CuSn), Nickel-aluminium bronze (CuAlNi), Duplex stainless steel (22Cr or 25Cr), Titanium Grade 2 (preferred for polluted ports and biofouling risk), Glass Reinforced Epoxy (GRE) for piping
- NOT ACCEPTABLE for seawater wetted surfaces: plain carbon steel, grey cast iron
- Heat exchanger tubes in tropical/polluted seawater: CuNi 70/30 (ASTM B111 C71500) or titanium Grade 2 (most resistant to erosion-corrosion and biofouling)

Freshwater circuit (HT/LT loops, expansion tank, internal piping):
- Carbon steel (seamless or ERW): acceptable with inhibited coolant treatment
- Copper alloys: compatible with treated freshwater; avoid direct galvanic contact with aluminium engine components
- Stainless steel 316L: suitable for all freshwater cooling service

Bimetallic (galvanic) corrosion prevention:
Where dissimilar metals join (e.g. steel pipe to bronze valve), insulating flanges, isolating sleeves, or cathodic protection shall be applied per DNV RP-0198.
整理说明：冷却水系统材料选型规范：海水侧须用铜镍合金/双相不锈钢/钛合金/GRE管（禁用碳钢/灰铸铁）；热带污染海域换热管推荐CuNi 70/30或钛合金；淡水侧可用碳钢（加抑制剂）；异种金属连接须防电化学腐蚀（绝缘法兰或阴极保护）。

乙二醇冷却液系统密封材料相容性要求
Cooling Water System Sealing Materials — Compatibility with Glycol-Based Coolants
(Based on engine manufacturer requirements and ISO 6194 seal material guidelines)

Elastomeric sealing material requirements for glycol-treated cooling circuits:
1. Elastomers exposed to ethylene glycol or propylene glycol coolant (typically 20–50% by volume) shall be selected for compatibility:
   PREFERRED: FKM (fluoroelastomer / Viton), PTFE, EPDM for dilute glycol (< 25%)
   AVOID: NBR (nitrile rubber) at glycol concentrations > 30% — swells and degrades, causing premature seal failure and system leakage
   AVOID: Natural rubber (NR), Neoprene (CR) with any glycol concentration
2. Pump shaft mechanical seals: carbon/ceramic or carbon/SiC face material combinations are preferred for glycol cooling service
3. Before adding glycol to a circuit previously run on plain water:
   - Renew all elastomeric O-rings, gaskets, and lip seals in the circuit
   - Flush the circuit thoroughly to remove plain-water scale and deposits
4. Inspection interval for elastomeric seals in glycol service: per manufacturer schedule, typically 2–4 years or at each coolant change

chunk_text:
主机停机后冷却水循环要求
Marine Diesel Engine — Post-Shutdown Cooling Water Circulation Requirements
(Based on MAN B&W Project Guide, Wärtsilä Service Manual, and IACS UR M51)

After main engine shutdown, cooling water circulation must be maintained to prevent thermal damage, coolant boiling, and cylinder liner distortion:

Normal planned shutdown:
- Continue HT cooling water circulation for minimum 20–30 minutes at reduced flow (electric standby pump or engine-driven pump at barring speed) until all cylinder jacket outlet temperatures fall below 60°C.

Emergency shutdown (high temperature trip / blackout):
- Immediate restart of electric cooling pump if available; circulation must not be interrupted for more than 5 minutes.
- Continue HT circulation until all cylinder outlet temperatures stabilise below 55°C. Typical duration: 45–90 minutes depending on engine size and thermal mass.

Turbocharger post-shutdown cooling:
- Continue cooling water flow to water-cooled turbocharger bearings for minimum 30 minutes post-shutdown to prevent bearing oil coking.

Post-shutdown electric cooling pump capacity:
- Minimum flow for post-shutdown cooling: 30–50% of rated MCR cooling flow is typically sufficient (confirm with engine manufacturer).

Engine restart restriction:
- Do not restart the engine until HT cooling water temperature has stabilised, and not before the minimum restart interval stated in the engine manual.
整理说明：主机停机后冷却水循环要求：正常停机循环至缸套出口<60°C（约20–30min）；紧急停机后循环至<55°C（45–90min）；增压器后冷却≥30min；备用电动泵须能提供30–50% MCR后冷却流量。

chunk_text:
冷却水系统初次投用前冲洗程序要求
Marine Cooling Water System — Pre-Service Flushing Requirements
(Based on MAN B&W Project Guide Flushing Procedure, DNV Rules, and standard shipyard commissioning practice)

Flushing of cooling water circuits is mandatory before first engine connection:

Objective: Remove welding slag, pipe scale, sand, construction debris from all cooling water piping before connecting to the main engine or sensitive equipment.

Flushing procedure:
1. BYPASS all sensitive equipment: temporarily disconnect or bypass the main engine coolant connections, temperature control valves, flow meters, and expansion tank internal fittings using temporary hoses or blind plates.
2. Fill system with clean fresh water (or inhibitor solution per coolant manufacturer guidance — do NOT use final glycol mix for flushing).
3. Circulate using cooling water pump(s) for minimum 2–4 hours at maximum available flow.
4. Minimum flushing velocity in all pipe branches: ≥ 1.5 m/s to ensure particle transport.
5. Drain completely; inspect and clean ALL strainer baskets and temporary flushing strainers.
6. If significant contamination found (rust scale, welding spatter), repeat flushing cycle.
7. Final fill: after satisfactory flush, fill with specified coolant formulation; vent all high points; check coolant quality (pH, inhibitor concentration, chloride content).
8. Document flushing results (water colour at drain, strainer inspection findings, number of flush cycles) in the commissioning record.
整理说明：冷却水系统初次使用前冲洗要求：旁通发动机和敏感设备，循环≥2–4小时，流速≥1.5 m/s，排水检查过滤器，必要时重复，按规定加注冷却液，冲洗记录入调试文件。
